projects.title: Brand Identity
projects.summary: Logo, colours, pattern and stationery for an Istanbul dental clinic, from the 2021 presentation to the 2022 guideline.

copy.text: A new identity for Saphire Dent, a dental clinic in Istanbul that treats patients from abroad. I joined the clinic in November 2020, and the identity was presented, in Arabic, in February 2021.

Designed the mark: a crown, a tooth and a diamond drawn as one icon, set over a SAPHIRE DENT wordmark. I tested the icon across colours and sizes, then built the rest of the kit from it: two brand colours, a diamond line pattern, circular seals, stationery, business cards, paper cups and staff ID cards. A second card direction, in gold foil on a dark card, followed in March 2021. Related: the clinic's website (chapter 05).

In January 2022 I set the logo and colours down in a guideline, with HEX, RGB and CMYK values, and the headed paper followed in February. The mark is still the clinic's logo and favicon on saphiredent.com.

copy.text: The clinic's main site had to do the job a brochure used to: explain treatments to patients who are choosing from abroad, in their own language, and make the next step obvious.

projects.title: Rebrand
projects.summary: Three logo directions, a deep red jasmine mark and a social media kit with post and story templates for a clinic.

copy.text: A clinic for dental, hair, face, body and bariatric treatments, for men and women, Arab and European patients alike. The new logo had to be “classy, confident, clear and identifiable” and express the name: yasmina is Arabic for jasmine.

Three logo directions, each written for a different patient: Calmness, Youth and Class. The clinic chose Class, an upright Y whose arms open into a jasmine sprig. Two colour rounds followed, and the clinic settled on a deep red. Around the mark I built the social media kit: cover and profile images, highlight and website icons, and before-and-after templates.
Templates the team fills in with each new case, so the feed stays on brand without a designer.

copy.text: Bespoke Clinics treats international patients in Istanbul for dental, hair, face, body and bariatric procedures. They wanted a brand that felt personal and premium rather than clinical, away from the cold blue and white of most clinics in the market, and a kit the staff could use from day one.

Stylescapes first, so the client could agree on a mood before any logo work. Then three monogram routes, each shown on signage, posters, vehicles and apparel. The client chose the first: a coral B and a peach C that share one stroke. Around it I built the palette, the stationery, social media templates and a WhatsApp kit for each sales consultant.
July 2022: the logo suite, stationery, social media templates and sales profiles.

projects.title: B2B Marketplace
projects.summary: Next.js front end for a B2B dental supply marketplace: five-category catalogue, trade pricing behind sign-in, RTL Arabic.

copy.text: Clinics buy consumables and equipment the way industry buys parts: by specification, in bulk, from suppliers they already deal with. So the model for the catalogue was an industrial supply house — McMaster-Carr — and not a consumer shop.

Designed and built the front end in Next.js: a five-category catalogue with brand, price and stock facets, product pages with trade pricing held behind sign-in, bulk-discount and seller panels, cart, and separate buyer and seller sign-up. Arabic is a full right-to-left build, not a translation layer.

277 commits before I paused it in June 2026. The front end is mine; it runs against a Java EE backend and ships an Expo mobile client from the same monorepo. The catalogue shown here is seeded demo data.

cover.cap: bazaardent.com — a trade marketplace for dental supply: prices open once you are signed in.

sections.title: Inside the Catalogue
sections.note: Trade buyers do not browse. They arrive knowing the part, and they want the price, the stock and the terms on one screen. That is why pricing sits behind sign-in, why the brand list carries its own search box, and why the whole catalogue was measured against McMaster-Carr rather than a consumer store. projects.title: Logo & Guidelines
projects.summary: A four-stroke mark and an Arabic guideline document for a UAE e-commerce platform, both brand colours specified.

copy.text: A new e-commerce platform aimed at young shoppers in the United Arab Emirates needed a mark that would survive being shrunk to an app icon and blown up to a billboard — and a set of rules its own team could follow without me in the room.

Drew the mark: four strokes that read as a wordmark at size and as a repeatable pattern when tiled. Then wrote the guideline document in Arabic — icon, colour, and typography plates, with Pantone, CMYK, RGB and hex specified for both brand colours so a printer in Dubai and a developer anywhere get the same red.
A small, complete identity: one mark, two colours, one typeface, and the document that keeps them consistent.
